claims.text: The studied material is CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Liquid-phase ultrafast laser ablation produces these nanoparticles with a narrow 3–5 nm size distribution and freshly exposed surfaces.
Bare CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles develop elemental surface segregation.
Elemental surface segregation produces a nonuniform surface-element distribution.
Surface segregation creates locally undercoordinated surface atoms.
Local undercoordination lowers cohesive energy and the energy barrier for atomic rearrangement.
The reduced barrier caused by undercoordination nucleates early premelting.
An immediately applied thin carbon or inert-oxide overlayer inhibits surface segregation.
Suppressing segregation with an overlayer preserves a more uniform surface structure and atomic-coordination environment.
The more uniform surface has greater local bonding strength and a higher barrier to atomic rearrangement.
Bare nanoparticles will exhibit an earlier onset of premelting than overlayer-coated nanoparticles.
Bare nanoparticles will exhibit a broader melting transition than overlayer-coated nanoparticles.
Overlayer-coated nanoparticles will exhibit delayed premelting and a sharper melting response.
The proposed segregation-controlled behavior should hold over the 3–8 nm particle-size range under the stated synthesis and atmospheric conditions.
Changes in particle size, synthesis method, surface chemistry, thermal conductivity, or interfacial heat transfer may independently alter premelting behavior.
A controlled comparison should use bare and coated particles with identical size distributions, heating atmospheres, and temperature ramp rates.
Failure of the coating to produce a statistically significant premelting delay, or attribution of the full difference to heat-transfer effects, would falsify the proposed segregation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that segregation develops during synthesis, whereas the proposed overlayer is deposited only after synthesis and is said to suppress segregation. If the relevant segregation has already occurred during synthesis, a post-synthesis coating cannot prevent its initial formation without an additional reversal or equilibration step.
